sections.html:
Sellers in DeSoto generally pick between hiring an agent, doing it alone and taking a cash offer on the house as it stands. Cash buys you speed and costs you some price.

Your property taxes go through Dallas County, with values set by the Dallas Central Appraisal District. Many local rules, though, are enforced by the city's code enforcement office. Rental registration and short-term rental permits are the two that investors ask about most.

  • Agent listing: the widest exposure, along with showings and a wait while the buyer's loan is approved.
  • Sell it yourself: no commission, but every form is yours to handle.
  • Cash purchase: a shorter timeline and no repair list, at less than a staged, repaired house might bring.

sections.h2: Rental registration for a tenant-occupied house
sections.html:
A house with a tenant falls under the city's Rental Registration and Inspection Program, which reaches every residential rental: single-family houses, duplexes, multi-family buildings, townhomes and manufactured homes.

Registration costs $10.00 per unit, and each unit is inspected every year. Registration itself does not have to be renewed annually if tenants and ownership stay the same. Inspections are scheduled with the city, and an inspector needs the tenant, the owner or a representative on site. Only exterior inspections happen without advance notice. Register through the city's Civic Access Portal, or by appointment for a paper form with Code Enforcement at 469-658-3067.

The program exists to preserve rental housing and to give staff a steadier way to press absentee and local landlords to fix violations. A buyer of a tenant-occupied house will want proof that registration is current and that the last inspection passed, and open violations tend to lower offers. If the portal does not show your property, email the city or leave a detailed message on the rental registration line, which is answered Monday through Thursday between 8:30 am and 10 am, with up to two business days for a reply.

Only an owner-occupied one-family or two-family dwelling qualifies, and it needs a registered permit. A short-term rental means overnight lodging for one to twenty-nine days, and the operator may not provide food or beverages.

Neighbors with a noise or parking complaint can use the city's online portal or call 800-685-1699, which is monitored around the clock. An approved operator receives a permit number by email, and it has to appear in advertisements and on booking sites.

Ordinance No. 2180-19 requires every operator to register and obtain a permit. The fee is $125 per property each year, and skipping registration can bring a citation with fines reaching $500 for each day. Applicants submit a sketched floor plan with room measurements and a site plan that shows the maximum number of vehicles that can park without blocking streets, sidewalks or alleys. Operators also collect and remit occupancy tax each month.

A buyer hoping to run a short-term rental cannot count on the rule fitting their plans, so send them to the city before they commit.

Check these with the city before paying, as fees get revised.

Begin with whatever shows the house is in good standing with the city. A rented house needs its registration confirmation and the result of the latest annual inspection. An owner who has run a short-term rental should find the emailed permit number and the record of monthly occupancy tax payments.

  • The latest tax statement, with confirmation of your homestead exemption at the appraisal district.
  • Any appraisal notice mailed in May and any protest paperwork.
  • The deed, plus releases for any earlier loans.
  • A written list of the repairs you already know about, which lets a cash buyer price them.

Organized records shorten a title search and make a written offer easier to judge. A buyer who sees open city violations or unknown liens will either ask for time or lower the number.

sections.h2: How Dallas County taxes work for a DeSoto seller
sections.html:
Appraisal is handled by the Dallas Central Appraisal District, which uses full market value and must look at each property again at least every three years. Notices for homes reappraised in a given year are mailed in May. Dallas County's tax office does the collecting.

To challenge a value, first sit down informally with an appraiser, then take a formal protest to the Appraisal Review Board if that fails. Filing an exemption is free, so call the appraisal district if any company asks you to pay for it. Your bill is due October 1, and after January 31 it is delinquent.

Statewide, school taxes drop by a $140,000 residence homestead exemption, and owners 65 or older gain another $60,000. DeSoto's other taxing units may add exemptions, so the county tax office can tell you what appears on your bill.

  • Ask for the current-year payoff amount well before closing.
  • Make sure the homestead exemption is on file.
  • Keep your last tax statement for the title company.

sections.h2: Inherited, in default or behind on taxes
sections.html:
Every one of these has its own deadline, and a sale can still happen if you act before it runs out. Heirs have four years to probate a will. Without a will, a small estate affidavit may be possible when the estate passes the state's tests, one of which is a $75,000 cap on assets, not counting homestead and exempt property.

A lender on a defaulted mortgage has to send a default notice first, and you can bring the loan current by paying the overdue amount within 20 days. After that an auction notice goes out, and the sale happens on a first Tuesday. The sale location is set by Dallas County, so the county clerk can tell you where notices are filed.

If property tax is delinquent, you may request a waiver of penalty and interest in writing, as long as you do it before the 181st day after the delinquency date and pay the tax within 21 days of learning of it. Start by asking the Dallas County tax office for the account history. Its Customer Care Center is at 214-653-7811 for tax questions, and the Dallas Central Appraisal District is at 214-631-0910 for appraisal and exemption questions.

When a buyer signs, the title company orders a title search and requests your lender's payoff. It also checks tax and lien records, so an unpaid city charge or an old lien release can surface here. Fix those quickly, since they are the usual cause of a delayed date.

Plan on signing the deed before a notary, handing over keys and openers, and cancelling or transferring utilities on closing day. Proceeds follow after the payoff and any tax share come out.

faqs.q: What is the DeSoto rental registration fee?
faqs.a: The fee is $10.00 per unit, with each side of a duplex counted as one unit. Every unit also needs an annual inspection.

faqs.q: What is the fine for an unregistered short-term rental in DeSoto?
faqs.a: A citation can carry fines reaching $500 for each day. Registration costs $125 per year for each property.
The Dallas Central Appraisal District, at 100 percent of fair market value, with a fresh look at each property at least every three years.

faqs.q: When are DeSoto property taxes due?
faqs.a: Bills are due October 1. After January 31 they are delinquent and penalty and interest accrue.

faqs.q: Do buyers need DeSoto's approval to rent a house they buy?
faqs.a: They must register it. A long-term rental goes through the rental registration program, while a short-term rental needs its own permit and has to be owner-occupied.
